Applied MUS
Applied Music: 32 credits required with a minimum of 12 credits at the 400 level. Approved courses include MUS 301, 302, 401, and 402. Students will enroll in 400-level lessons after passing their second-year assessment.

Music Ensemble or MUS 441
Music Ensemble or MUS 441: Pianists must complete a minimum of 8 ensemble credits. This requirement includes a minimum of 6 credits of MUS 441 (collaborative piano) and 2 credits of any other vocal or instrumental ensemble. To fulfill the [ARTS] UCORE requirement, 3 credits of ensemble courses designated as ARTS must be completed.

Students must complete a minimum of 6 credits of electives outside of MUS and UCORE requirements.  Please consult with advisor for elective selection.

Senior Full Recital

Each student desiring to pursue a music major at WSU must have an audition with the studio teacher of the major instrument or voice of intended study, and in the case of multiple teachers in the studio, with the area coordinator. Faculty and students are encouraged to set up an audition before the semester, use the first lesson as an audition, or use the ensemble placement audition as the audition. 

To be admitted as a major pursuing any degree in music, students must meet the following criteria:

1. Successfully audition into 300-level lessons on their major instrument or voice.

2. Enroll in MUS 251 and 252 or be approved to receive transfer credit by the Music Theory Area Coordinator. 

Requirements include:  Accompany a junior, senior, or graduate recital; piano proficiency exam; second-year assessment; junior recital; senior recital; achieve a cumulative 2.5 GPA and a grade of C or better in all music classes. Pianists must complete a minimum of 8 ensemble credits. This requirement includes a minimum of 6 credits of MUS 441 (collaborative piano) and 2 credits of any other vocal or instrumental ensemble. Any exceptions must be arranged with the instructor of the applied lessons. 

Only 9 credits of MUS courses can be used to fulfill UCORE requirements.
